stories.title: Greenland forces Trump-linked US oil firm to delay drilling
stories.summary: US envoy had claim Americans could be extracting crude by as early as next year Greenland authorities have forced a US oil company connected to Donald Trump to postpone drilling wells in the Arctic territory, defying claims by the US president’s envoy that Americans could be extracting crude by next year. Amid Trump’s imperialist threats, tensions have been rising on Greenland’s eastern coast after the oil company brought drilling equipment ashore in July without permission, drawing a “strong warning” from the government. stories.title: Former Mexican governor charged in case of 43 students who vanished in 2014
stories.summary: Ángel Aguirre indicted in case that rocked Mexico and became symbol of its brutal cartel violence The former governor of Guerrero state in Mexico has been formally charged over his alleged involvement in the disappearance of 43 students in 2014, a case that has become a symbol of the country’s brutal cartel violence and government impunity. Ángel Aguirre, who was arrested last week , is accused of forced disappearance and obstruction of justice for ordering the destruction of surveillance tapes that may have shed light on what happened to the students from the Ayotzinapa teacher training college on the night of 26 September 2014. stories.summary: Suit alleges subscription offer aims to sell privileged access to information generated in president’s official capacity Donald Trump has been sued after a subscription service charging up to $100,000 a month for early access to his posts on his Truth Social platform sparked allegations of corruption. stories.title: Yorkshire crowds gather for 'incredible' eclipse
stories.summary: People gather in York, Leeds and Bradford to view the most significant solar eclipse since 1999.
stories.post: 📰 NEWS: Yorkshire crowds gather for 'incredible' eclipse. People gather in York, Leeds and Bradford to view the most significant solar eclipse since 1999. Source: BBC Science.
article_sentences: Crowds have gathered across Yorkshire to view the most significant solar eclipse since 1999.
An eclipse happens when the Sun, Moon and Earth are in alignment.
The Moon casts a shadow on the Earth as it passes between the two, completely or partially blocking out the Sun.
At Beetle Bank Farm in York, the York Astronomical Society had telescopes set up, while families made pinhole cameras and donned their solar glasses.
Brian Jones from the astronomical society said it was "lovely" to be among about 200 people sharing the rare event.
"The universe is there to be shared.
I've been interested since I was about five, and it gets you," he said.
"You're made of star stuff - everything in your body comes from a star, so you're looking back at family history."
Brother Max said he felt it "had gone really cold".
"The Sun generates all the heat and the Moon is blocking out the Sun," he explained.
Their mum Tracey said she felt "really lucky" to see a second solar eclipse in her lifetime.
